item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is narrowly preferable because its retry verification more closely models the reported os.Open workflow and checks byte-for-byte replay. Neither patch is merge-ready: both bypass FilesService.Add and make explicitly out-of-scope retry-transport changes.","reasons":["A retries Upload using an open file and verifies that the complete encoded multipart body is identical across attempts; B's retry test uses strings.NewReader, while its open-file test does not exercise retry.","A defensively avoids setting ContentLength when the seek end precedes the starting offset; B assigns end-start unconditionally.","A introduces somewhat less unnecessary helper and test machinery around the out-of-scope RawClient behavior.","Both correctly add the required Upload signature, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validate inputs, and propagate helper errors."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through Add as explicitly required.","The RawClient seek/replay and ownership changes alter Add, Update, and Raw behavior despite the contract prohibiting unrelated retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.","No Upload test covers a source reader returning an error; option forwarding is also not directly verified."],"risks_b":["Upload likewise duplicates Add rather than delegating to it.","wireSeekableRequestBody silently suppresses seek failures and may leave a reader repositioned after a failed restoration; it can also assign a negative ContentLength.","The Upload retry test does not use streamed/open-file content or explicitly set RetryAllMethods as in the reported scenario, and there is no source-reader error test."]}
